days.desc: 6 miles total at conversational effort. Let pace follow recovery and conditions; do not force a fixed 9:30 pace. progressionRule: Treat this as a conditional plan, not mileage owed. The initial 31-mile week and 12-mile run are aggressive compared with the recent shared history. Advance only when completed training, normal easy effort and recovery support the next step; repeat or reduce the last tolerated load if training is missed or recovery deteriorates. Never make up missed miles or override recovery reductions to hit a target. Keep Friday and Sunday as rest days, Saturday long runs, and at most one structured quality workout per week. No faster work or hard strength October 26 week. January 2 optional goal-pace finish replaces Thursday quality. January 14 and 21 are easy-only before the longest runs. January 16 and 23 are conditional 20- and 22-mile ceilings, capped at 3h30; all other long runs retain a three-hour cap. Keep the three-week taper. Race is Sunday February 14. Requested 50- and 52-mile peak weeks are conditional upper targets, not mandatory totals or established capacity. Lead-in is 40, 44, then 36 miles. Do not jump to either peak after missed training, persistent fatigue, worsening pain or altered running mechanics. Added volume is easy; do not add speed or extend long runs beyond their existing ceilings. Keep the taper even if peak targets are missed.
qualityRule: Every faster workout includes easy warm-up and cool-down inside the stated daily distance. Use the planned workout only with no pain, normal easy-running effort and recovery, and two consistent preceding weeks. Otherwise complete the day easy or follow a recovery reduction. Goal-pace blocks are controlled practice, never a requirement to hold an unsustainable pace.

checkpoints.title: Controlled 20-minute benchmark
checkpoints.review: Run the scheduled 20 minutes at a controlled hard effort, not an all-out time trial. Record average pace, effort, and next-day recovery. Use this to set current tempo effort; do not infer a marathon prediction from it.

checkpoints.title: 3:40 readiness review
checkpoints.review: Review consistency, recovery, the January 2 long run, and how 8:23–8:35 blocks felt. Keep 3:40 as the A goal only if the pace is controlled and endurance is progressing. Difficulty at goal pace is a reason to adjust the race target, not force faster easy runs.

racePreparation.trainingPriority: Consistent weeks and recovery take priority over hitting a higher peak number. Keep long runs mostly easy; practice controlled goal-pace blocks only when readiness conditions are met.
racePreparation.fuelPractice: For runs lasting 1–2.5 hours, build toward 30–60 g carbohydrate per hour using familiar products. For longer race-duration efforts, higher intakes may help but require gradual gut training and individual tolerance; never introduce an untested intake on race day.
racePreparation.goalReview: Use late-December/January training, a suitable tune-up race if available, and long-run recovery to review the A goal. Shorter-race equivalence is supportive evidence only; marathon endurance and fueling must also support the target.
